label: Identify testable expectations in a requirement
label_nl: Identify testable expectations in a requirement
definition: Given a short requirement, identify the actor or component, triggering condition, expected observable outcome, and any stated constraint; mark ambiguities rather than inventing expected behavior.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner who can read basic software requirements

assessment.method: short scenario exercise
criteria: extracts an observable outcome
preserves stated constraints
flags missing or ambiguous expectations

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis

label: Turn an expected behavior into a test case
label_nl: Turn an expected behavior into a test case
definition: Specify a test's preconditions, input or action, and expected result so another person can perform the check and judge its outcome.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner who understands basic requirements

assessment.method: write test cases for a small feature
criteria: covers the stated behavior
includes relevant preconditions and inputs
states an observable expected result
avoids unsupported assumptions

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis

label: Prepare a controlled test condition
label_nl: Prepare a controlled test condition
definition: Select or set up the software version, account or fixture, data, and environment needed to run a specified test, while recording material setup differences.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate; practical setup varies by tool and environment

assessment.method: supervised practical setup
criteria: uses the requested version and data
sets up the stated preconditions
records deviations
does not use real personal data in the exercise

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis

label: Execute a test and record what happened
label_nl: Execute a test and record what happened
definition: Perform the specified actions in order and record the actual observable result, including enough context to distinguish observation from interpretation.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a small, guided test environment

assessment.method: observed practical demonstration
criteria: follows the test steps
records actual behavior accurately
captures relevant version and test data
does not label an outcome as a defect before comparison

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis

label: Compare an observation with a stated expectation
label_nl: Compare an observation with a stated expectation
definition: Compare an observed result against an explicit expected result and classify it as matching, differing, or inconclusive, citing the evidence for that classification.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate; the cognitive operation is proposed as reusable, while domain criteria remain contextual

assessment.method: case classification exercise
criteria: uses the stated expectation as the comparison basis
distinguishes mismatch from missing evidence
points to the observed evidence
does not infer a cause from mismatch alone

reusability.hypothesis: The comparison operation may recur in reconciliation, inspection, and quality control. No cross-role mappings are asserted in this pilot.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis

label: Describe a reproducible software defect
label_nl: Describe a reproducible software defect
definition: Write a concise defect report with environment or version, preconditions, steps, expected result, actual result, and supporting evidence so another person can attempt to reproduce it.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate; depends on the reporting tool and complexity of the defect

assessment.method: defect-report authoring and peer reproduction
criteria: includes required context
steps are ordered and actionable
expected and actual results are separated
evidence supports the claim
a peer can reproduce or identify what information is missing

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis

label: Identify the stated tax base and rate
label_nl: Identify the stated tax base and rate
definition: Given a transaction example and a supplied, dated reference for the named jurisdiction, identify the amount to which tax applies and the stated rate. Flag missing jurisdiction, date, or rule information instead of guessing.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites

assessment.method: short scenario or worked calculation
criteria: identifies the base amount from the supplied facts
finds the rate in the supplied reference
checks that jurisdiction and effective date are stated
flags missing or conflicting information

reusability.hypothesis: This unit does not teach legal interpretation or determine which tax rule applies in a real case.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis; requires practitioner and learning-design review

label: Interpret a percentage as parts per hundred
label_nl: Interpret a percentage as parts per hundred
definition: Explain a stated percentage as a ratio with denominator 100 and connect it to a simple visual or numerical example.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites

assessment.method: short scenario or worked calculation
criteria: interprets p% as p out of 100
matches common percentages to equivalent simple fractions or visuals
distinguishes the percentage from the amount it applies to

reusability.hypothesis: Candidate for reuse across domains; no additional occupation mappings are asserted.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis; requires practitioner and learning-design review

label: Convert a percentage to a decimal factor
label_nl: Convert a percentage to a decimal factor
definition: Convert a percentage into an equivalent decimal factor suitable for multiplying an amount, preserving the value.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites

assessment.method: short scenario or worked calculation
criteria: moves between percent and decimal forms correctly
checks equivalence using parts per hundred
preserves place value for values below and above 100%

reusability.hypothesis: Candidate for reuse across domains; no additional occupation mappings are asserted.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis; requires practitioner and learning-design review

label: Calculate a percentage of an amount
label_nl: Calculate a percentage of an amount
definition: Calculate a stated percentage of a given amount by multiplying the amount by the equivalent decimal factor and present the result with units or currency.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites

assessment.method: short scenario or worked calculation
criteria: uses the supplied amount and percentage
chooses the equivalent decimal factor correctly
performs the multiplication accurately
labels the result with the appropriate unit

reusability.hypothesis: Candidate for reuse across domains. This is not a claim that the same proficiency standard applies in every occupation.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis; requires practitioner and learning-design review

label: Estimate a percentage result to check its size
label_nl: Estimate a percentage result to check its size
definition: Use a benchmark or rounded estimate to decide whether a calculated percentage is in a plausible range before accepting it.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites

assessment.method: short scenario or worked calculation
criteria: selects a useful benchmark such as 10%, 25%, or 50%
estimates the expected magnitude
identifies a result outside the plausible range
does not treat a plausibility check as proof of exactness

reusability.hypothesis: Candidate for reuse in other calculation contexts; no other job mappings are asserted.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis; requires practitioner and learning-design review

label: Apply a stated rounding rule and record the calculation
label_nl: Apply a stated rounding rule and record the calculation
definition: Apply the rounding rule supplied for the exercise, record the base, rate, unrounded calculation, rounded result, and source reference so another person can review the calculation.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites

assessment.method: short scenario or worked calculation
criteria: uses the supplied rounding rule consistently
records the base and rate
keeps calculation and rounded result distinguishable
provides enough information for another person to reproduce the arithmetic

reusability.hypothesis: The applicable legal or accounting rule must come from an authoritative, current source.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis; requires practitioner and learning-design review

label: Select an instrument and range for a specified electrical check
label_nl: Select an instrument and range for a specified electrical check
definition: Given a supplied electrical test instruction, choose a suitable measurement instrument, setting, and range, and state what value or property the check is intended to observe.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites

assessment.method: supervised practical demonstration with a supplied test instruction
criteria: matches the instrument and range to the named measurement
uses the supplied instruction rather than guessing the test objective
checks for stated calibration or inspection status
explains what reading will be recorded

reusability.hypothesis: Instrument selection is equipment-specific and requires supervised practical review.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis; requires qualified electrical practitioner and learning-design review

label: Perform and record an electrical measurement using a supplied safe method
label_nl: Perform and record an electrical measurement using a supplied safe method
definition: Under appropriate supervision, follow an approved test procedure to take a specified electrical measurement, then record the observed value, unit, instrument, range, and relevant setup.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites

assessment.method: supervised practical demonstration with a supplied test instruction
criteria: follows the supplied safety and test procedure
uses the selected instrument and range correctly
records the observed value and unit accurately
records relevant setup and flags an invalid or uncertain measurement

reusability.hypothesis: Safety-critical practical performance. This draft is not a substitute for site-specific authorization or supervision.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis; requires qualified electrical practitioner and learning-design review

label: Compare an electrical reading with specified limits
label_nl: Compare an electrical reading with specified limits
definition: Compare a recorded electrical reading, including its unit and relevant measurement resolution, with a stated expected value or permitted range and classify it as within range, outside range, or inconclusive.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites

assessment.method: supervised practical demonstration with a supplied test instruction
criteria: checks that the measured quantity and unit match the stated limit
compares the reading with the specified range
flags a result as inconclusive where resolution or conditions do not support a decision
does not infer a fault cause from an out-of-range result

reusability.hypothesis: This is a context-specific specialization of the Atlas capability “Compare an observation with a stated expectation”; the general capability alone does not establish electrical testing competence.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis; requires qualified electrical practitioner and learning-design review

label: Count up to ten objects and match the total to a numeral
label_nl: Count up to ten objects and match the total to a numeral
definition: Count a set of up to ten objects by assigning one count word to each object, then state the total and select its matching numeral.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites

assessment.method: short practical or worked-number demonstration
criteria: counts each object exactly once
states the final count as the set size
matches quantities up to ten to numerals
recognizes when an object was skipped or counted twice

reusability.hypothesis: Foundational numeracy outcome with potential cross-context use; no occupation mappings asserted in this release.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis; learning-time range requires learner calibration

label: Add single-digit quantities within ten
label_nl: Add single-digit quantities within ten
definition: Combine two groups of objects with a total no greater than ten and determine the sum by counting all, counting on, or a known addition fact.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites

assessment.method: short practical or worked-number demonstration
criteria: models both addends and the combined set
solves examples including 1 + 1 = 2
states the sum and matches it to a numeral
checks the result by recounting or using a related fact

reusability.hypothesis: Foundational numeracy outcome with potential cross-context use; no occupation mappings asserted in this release.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis; learning-time range requires learner calibration

label: Add whole numbers within twenty
label_nl: Add whole numbers within twenty
definition: Find sums of whole numbers with totals up to twenty using concrete objects, counting on, decomposing numbers, or a known fact, and explain or show the chosen method.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites

assessment.method: short practical or worked-number demonstration
criteria: selects a workable addition strategy
keeps track of both addends
computes the total accurately
uses a second representation or check when uncertain

reusability.hypothesis: Foundational numeracy outcome with potential cross-context use; no occupation mappings asserted in this release.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis; learning-time range requires learner calibration

label: Represent multiplication as equal groups
label_nl: Represent multiplication as equal groups
definition: Represent a multiplication expression with equal groups, an array, or repeated addition and identify the number of groups, the amount in each group, and the total.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites

assessment.method: short practical or worked-number demonstration
criteria: builds equal-sized groups from the expression
distinguishes number of groups from group size
writes or explains a matching repeated-addition expression
finds the total for small examples

reusability.hypothesis: Foundational numeracy outcome with potential cross-context use; no occupation mappings asserted in this release.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis; learning-time range requires learner calibration

label: Multiply a two-digit whole number by a one-digit factor
label_nl: Multiply a two-digit whole number by a one-digit factor
definition: Calculate products of a two-digit whole number and a one-digit whole number by using equal groups, known facts, or place-value decomposition, and show how the method preserves the value.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites

assessment.method: short practical or worked-number demonstration
criteria: identifies the two factors in a two-digit-by-one-digit multiplication
chooses a valid multiplication strategy
computes the product accurately
checks the magnitude with an estimate or a second method

reusability.hypothesis: Foundational numeracy outcome with potential cross-context use; no occupation mappings asserted in this release.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis; learning-time range requires learner calibration

label: Interpret decimal place value through hundredths
label_nl: Interpret decimal place value through hundredths
definition: Read, represent, and compare decimal numbers through hundredths by connecting digits to ones, tenths, and hundredths and to equivalent fractions or visual models.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites

assessment.method: short practical or worked-number demonstration
criteria: identifies the value represented by each digit
places decimal values correctly on a number line or model
compares two decimals using place value
connects tenths and hundredths to fractions with denominators 10 and 100

reusability.hypothesis: Foundational numeracy outcome with potential cross-context use; no occupation mappings asserted in this release.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis; learning-time range requires learner calibration

label: Scale an integer product using a decimal factor
label_nl: Scale an integer product using a decimal factor
definition: Use place value or an equivalent fraction to calculate a whole-number amount multiplied by a decimal factor to hundredths, and explain the scale applied to the integer product.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites

assessment.method: short practical or worked-number demonstration
criteria: uses the supplied decimal factor without changing its value
connects the calculation to an equivalent fraction or place-value model
places the decimal point based on the scale rather than guesswork
checks the result against a rough estimate

reusability.hypothesis: Foundational numeracy outcome with potential cross-context use; no occupation mappings asserted in this release.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored decomposition hypothesis; learning-time range requires learner calibration

label: Prepare a basic observation encounter from a supplied care plan
label_nl: Een observatiemoment voorbereiden aan de hand van een zorgplan
definition: In a supervised simulation, check the supplied instruction and local procedure, confirm the person using the setting’s identification process, explain the observation, attend to privacy and comfort, and prepare the specified equipment.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative supervised simulation estimate; excludes workplace authorization and sign-off

assessment.method: observed simulation with supplied checklist
criteria: follows the supplied identification and consent process
explains the observation in understandable language and responds to discomfort
selects the specified device and checks readiness using its supplied instructions
uses the local hand-hygiene and safety procedure
pauses and seeks qualified help when instructions or the person’s condition make proceeding unclear

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored proposal; exact practice must follow current employer policy and qualified supervision.

label: Perform an assigned basic observation using its supplied procedure
label_nl: Een toegewezen basisobservatie uitvoeren volgens de aangeleverde procedure
definition: In a supervised simulation, perform one assigned basic observation using the device-specific, current procedure supplied for that scenario; do not infer a diagnosis or substitute a remembered technique for the supplied procedure.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for one defined measurement procedure in supervised simulation

assessment.method: observed skills demonstration using a device-specific checklist
criteria: uses the supplied procedure and device instructions in the stated order
records or states when the reading could not be obtained reliably
does not invent thresholds, diagnose, or alter the procedure
stops and seeks qualified help if the situation is outside the supplied scenario

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored proposal; measurement procedures and scope require qualified clinical review.

label: Record an observation with its time, units and context
label_nl: Een observatie vastleggen met tijdstip, eenheid en context
definition: Enter a supplied or simulated observation accurately in the designated record, preserving its value, unit, time, measurement context and any stated limitation; distinguish observed facts from interpretation.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate using a supplied record template

assessment.method: recording exercise using simulated observations
criteria: transcribes the value and unit accurately
includes the time and required context
marks missing or unreliable readings instead of guessing
separates direct observations from interpretation

reusability.hypothesis: Accurate, contextual recording may transfer across healthcare settings and other safety-critical work. This is a reuse hypothesis only; no additional ESCO occupation mapping is asserted.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored proposal; documentation format and privacy rules require local review.

label: Compare an observation with supplied escalation criteria
label_nl: Een observatie vergelijken met aangeleverde opschalingscriteria
definition: Compare a simulated observation, or stated change from baseline, only with the explicit criteria supplied in the scenario; identify a match or uncertainty without making a diagnosis.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate using fictional cases and supplied criteria

assessment.method: scenario classification exercise
criteria: uses the supplied criterion without changing or generalizing it
correctly identifies whether the case meets the stated trigger
flags missing, conflicting or uncertain information
does not diagnose or delay escalation while seeking certainty

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored proposal; fictional criteria only. Real thresholds and escalation rules must come from current local protocols.

label: Report a concerning observation through the supplied escalation route
label_nl: Een zorgelijke observatie melden via de aangeleverde escalatieroute
definition: In a simulated handover, promptly pass the observed facts, time, relevant context, supplied trigger and action already taken to the designated qualified person using the route specified in the scenario.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative role-play estimate using a supplied local escalation route

assessment.method: role-play handover with a supplied scenario card
criteria: uses the stated route and urgency from the scenario
communicates the observed value, unit, time and relevant change clearly
states uncertainty and action already taken
requests confirmation or further direction when required by the supplied procedure

reusability.hypothesis: Concise factual handover may transfer across healthcare settings and other safety-critical work. The proposed route and scope remain context-specific; no additional ESCO mappings are asserted.

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored proposal; use only under qualified supervision and current local escalation policy.

label: Extract a user need and its stated constraints
label_nl: Een gebruikersbehoefte en de genoemde randvoorwaarden uitwerken
definition: Given a short fictional request, identify who needs what outcome, in which situation, and the constraints explicitly stated. Separate evidence from assumptions and list questions that need clarification.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites; recalibration needed

assessment.method: short scenario brief
criteria: identifies the user and desired outcome
quotes or restates each stated constraint accurately
labels assumptions and unresolved questions separately

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored learning-design proposal informed by ESCO software-developer capabilities and ACM/IEEE software-engineering curriculum areas; not an ESCO record or expert-validated prerequisite.

label: Write observable acceptance conditions for a software requirement
label_nl: Waarneembare acceptatievoorwaarden voor een software-eis formuleren
definition: Rewrite one clarified requirement as observable conditions, including normal input, a boundary case, and an invalid or unavailable input where relevant. Do not silently decide unspecified behavior.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites; recalibration needed

assessment.method: requirement-to-examples exercise
criteria: each condition describes observable behavior
includes at least one boundary or failure case
flags behavior that still needs a product decision

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored learning-design proposal informed by ESCO software-developer capabilities and ACM/IEEE software-engineering curriculum areas; not an ESCO record or expert-validated prerequisite.

label: Map a small feature as a flowchart
label_nl: De besturingsstroom van een kleine functie als stroomschema weergeven
definition: Represent a small feature as ordered steps, decisions, and outcomes in a flowchart; check that each stated acceptance condition has a path through the model.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites; recalibration needed

assessment.method: flowchart exercise
criteria: uses decision branches for conditional behavior
shows an outcome for each represented path
connects paths to stated acceptance conditions

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored learning-design proposal informed by ESCO software-developer capabilities and ACM/IEEE software-engineering curriculum areas; not an ESCO record or expert-validated prerequisite.

label: Separate responsibilities in a small feature design
label_nl: Verantwoordelijkheden in het ontwerp van een kleine functie scheiden
definition: Given a small feature, sketch its inputs, outputs, state changes, and responsibilities. Compare two simple designs and explain the trade-off using a supplied design principle or pattern rather than applying a named pattern by rote.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites; recalibration needed

assessment.method: annotated design sketch
criteria: names the responsibility handled by each part
shows how information crosses the boundary
explains one trade-off and one consequence of the chosen design

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored learning-design proposal informed by ESCO software-developer capabilities and ACM/IEEE software-engineering curriculum areas; not an ESCO record or expert-validated prerequisite.

label: Build a thin software prototype from a specification
label_nl: Een dunne softwareprototypeversie vanuit een specificatie bouwen
definition: Implement one narrow, runnable slice of a supplied feature that demonstrates the specified input-to-output behavior; keep unsupported behavior explicit and avoid treating the prototype as production-ready.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites; recalibration needed

assessment.method: small runnable prototype
criteria: runs the demonstrated happy path
shows at least one boundary or failure behavior
states what remains simulated, incomplete, or unsafe for production

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored learning-design proposal informed by ESCO software-developer capabilities and ACM/IEEE software-engineering curriculum areas; not an ESCO record or expert-validated prerequisite.

label: Implement and explain a small function
label_nl: Een kleine functie implementeren en toelichten
definition: Implement a small function against supplied examples in one available language, using clear names and explicit input/output behavior. Explain the logic and check the result against examples; the outcome is language-neutral.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites; recalibration needed

assessment.method: code-and-explanation exercise
criteria: implementation matches the supplied examples
explains how control and data flow through the function
identifies one limitation or unhandled case

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored learning-design proposal informed by ESCO software-developer capabilities and ACM/IEEE software-engineering curriculum areas; not an ESCO record or expert-validated prerequisite.

label: Record and review a code change with version control
label_nl: Een codewijziging met versiebeheer vastleggen en beoordelen
definition: In a disposable practice repository, inspect the current change, create a focused commit with a useful message, and review the diff to confirm that only intended files and changes are included.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites; recalibration needed

assessment.method: guided repository exercise
criteria: distinguishes working changes from the recorded commit
writes a message that summarizes intent
uses the diff to catch an unintended change

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored learning-design proposal informed by ESCO software-developer capabilities and ACM/IEEE software-engineering curriculum areas; not an ESCO record or expert-validated prerequisite.

label: Trace a software fault with debugging tools
label_nl: Een softwarefout met debughulpmiddelen traceren
definition: Use a supplied reproducible failure and a debugger or equivalent inspection tool to follow execution, inspect relevant values, form a fault hypothesis, and verify it with a minimal change or focused check.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites; recalibration needed

assessment.method: debugging lab
criteria: reproduces the stated failure before changing code
uses observed program state to support a fault hypothesis
checks whether the proposed change addresses the reproduction

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored learning-design proposal informed by ESCO software-developer capabilities and ACM/IEEE software-engineering curriculum areas; not an ESCO record or expert-validated prerequisite.

label: Use a software library through its documented interface
label_nl: Een softwarebibliotheek via de gedocumenteerde interface gebruiken
definition: Choose a library supplied for a small task, consult its documentation, call only the needed interface, and state assumptions, version, and any behavior delegated to the dependency.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites; recalibration needed

assessment.method: library-use exercise
criteria: selects an interface relevant to the task
demonstrates a call with expected input and output
records the dependency and one limitation or risk

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored learning-design proposal informed by ESCO software-developer capabilities and ACM/IEEE software-engineering curriculum areas; not an ESCO record or expert-validated prerequisite.

label: Document technical behavior and a change
label_nl: Technisch gedrag en een wijziging documenteren
definition: Write a concise technical note for a small change: its purpose, inputs and outputs, important decisions, how to run or verify it, and known limitations. Link claims to the implemented behavior or supplied evidence.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites; recalibration needed

assessment.method: technical note
criteria: another learner can identify the purpose and expected behavior
run or verification steps are actionable
known limitations are separated from confirmed behavior

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored learning-design proposal informed by ESCO software-developer capabilities and ACM/IEEE software-engineering curriculum areas; not an ESCO record or expert-validated prerequisite.

label: Revise a prototype from clarified feedback
label_nl: Een prototype herzien op basis van verduidelijkte feedback
definition: Given feedback on a prototype, distinguish a requested outcome from a suggested implementation, ask for clarification where needed, and revise one acceptance condition and the smallest affected feature slice.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites; recalibration needed

assessment.method: feedback-to-change exercise
criteria: records the feedback without treating a proposed solution as a requirement
identifies the affected acceptance condition
shows the revised behavior and its impact

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored learning-design proposal informed by ESCO software-developer capabilities and ACM/IEEE software-engineering curriculum areas; not an ESCO record or expert-validated prerequisite.

label: Maintain trace links in a software engineering tool
label_nl: Een herleidbare verbinding bijhouden in een software-engineeringtool
definition: Use a supplied requirements or design workspace to link one requirement to its model, implementation task and verification evidence; identify missing links without treating a tool record as proof of correctness.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites; not empirically calibrated

assessment.method: traceability review
criteria: links each artifact to the correct requirement
finds a missing or stale relationship
states what the link does and does not prove

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored proposal informed by ESCO v1.2.1 capability label and ACM/IEEE CS2023 software-engineering curriculum areas; apply the stated sandbox, supplied evidence and review boundaries.

label: Compare engineering tool views for consistency
label_nl: Weergaven in een engineeringtool op samenhang controleren
definition: Compare two supplied project views, such as a requirements list and component model, and record conflicts, omissions and the next owner/action.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites; not empirically calibrated

assessment.method: tool workspace exercise
criteria: identifies a concrete conflict or omission
records a reproducible location or identifier
assigns a clear follow-up action

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored proposal informed by ESCO v1.2.1 capability label and ACM/IEEE CS2023 software-engineering curriculum areas; apply the stated sandbox, supplied evidence and review boundaries.

label: Choose a lightweight workflow for a bounded change
label_nl: Een eenvoudige werkwijze kiezen voor een afgebakende wijziging
definition: Select a supplied development workflow that fits a small change, then identify the work, review and verification checkpoints it requires.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites; not empirically calibrated

assessment.method: workflow-selection scenario
criteria: names the change and relevant constraints
selects checkpoints that produce reviewable evidence
explains one risk the workflow addresses

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored proposal informed by ESCO v1.2.1 capability label and ACM/IEEE CS2023 software-engineering curriculum areas; apply the stated sandbox, supplied evidence and review boundaries.

label: Prepare a change for peer review
label_nl: Een wijziging voorbereiden voor collegiale beoordeling
definition: Package a small change with its purpose, scope, tests and known risks so a reviewer can assess it without inferring unstated requirements.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites; not empirically calibrated

assessment.method: review-ready change exercise
criteria: summarizes purpose and scope
links relevant verification evidence
calls out an unresolved risk or decision

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored proposal informed by ESCO v1.2.1 capability label and ACM/IEEE CS2023 software-engineering curriculum areas; apply the stated sandbox, supplied evidence and review boundaries.

label: Close a software change with traceable evidence
label_nl: Een softwarewijziging met herleidbaar bewijs afronden
definition: Record the accepted change, verification result and follow-up items in a supplied project workflow; distinguish completed work from deferred work.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites; not empirically calibrated

assessment.method: change-record exercise
criteria: records the verified result and its evidence
lists deferred work separately
leaves a traceable status

evidence_basis: Atlas-authored proposal informed by ESCO v1.2.1 capability label and ACM/IEEE CS2023 software-engineering curriculum areas; apply the stated sandbox, supplied evidence and review boundaries.

label: Map a source-to-target data transformation
label_nl: Een bron-doeltransformatie voor gegevens uitwerken
definition: For a fictional migration, document source fields, target fields, conversions, defaults, rejected values and assumptions before automating any transformation.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative estimate for a learner meeting stated prerequisites; not empirically calibrated

assessment.method: mapping worksheet
criteria: maps each required target field to a source or explicit rule
flags lossy or ambiguous conversions
separates defaults from observed source values

criteria: separates stated information from assumptions
recognizes differing perspectives and access needs
identifies a respectful way to check preferences

label: Notice and respond to early communication signals
label_nl: Notice and respond to early communication signals
definition: In a short video or fictional observation, notice a young child’s gaze, movement, vocalization, gesture, sign, or use of a communication aid. Describe a warm response that follows the child’s focus and allows time for a reply.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative guided play or scenario activity; not validated

assessment.method: Fictional caregiver scenario, video observation, or accessible play demonstration
criteria: notices more than spoken words as possible communication
describes a responsive, non-intrusive return
allows time and recognizes when the child signals to pause

evidence_basis: Harvard Center on the Developing Child serve-and-return guidance and ASHA early communication milestones inform this draft. Signals and interaction styles vary; this is not a diagnostic checklist.

label: Share attention and take communicative turns
label_nl: Share attention and take communicative turns
definition: Using a familiar play or daily-routine example, practice following the child’s interest, taking a brief turn, pausing, and responding to the child’s next signal in the communication modes available to them.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative guided play or scenario activity; not validated

assessment.method: Fictional caregiver scenario, video observation, or accessible play demonstration
criteria: follows the child’s focus rather than demanding eye contact
creates a reciprocal opportunity to communicate
adapts timing and sensory or access demands

evidence_basis: ASHA milestones and Harvard serve-and-return guidance inform this flexible practice activity.

label: Connect familiar words or symbols with meaning
label_nl: Connect familiar words or symbols with meaning
definition: Use a familiar object, action, person, or routine to model a meaningful word, sign, gesture, picture, or AAC symbol. Observe how the child responds and keep the interaction natural and pressure-free.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative guided play or scenario activity; not validated

assessment.method: Fictional caregiver scenario, video observation, or accessible play demonstration
criteria: uses a meaningful referent and an accessible communication form
models rather than requiring imitation
recognizes a response in any available mode

evidence_basis: ASHA early communication milestones and AAC early-intervention guidance inform this draft. AAC can be introduced without prerequisite skills.

label_nl: Support a first meaningful word, sign, or AAC message
definition: In a fictional caregiver scenario, identify how to notice and respond to a child’s first meaningful spoken word, sign, gesture, picture choice, or AAC symbol. Practice acknowledging the message and expanding the interaction without requiring speech.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative guided play or scenario activity; not validated

assessment.method: Fictional caregiver scenario, video observation, or accessible play demonstration
criteria: accepts the child’s current communication mode
responds to the meaning rather than correcting form
does not withhold AAC or other communication supports pending speech

evidence_basis: ASHA communication milestones and its AAC early-intervention guidance inform this draft; there is no prerequisite for considering AAC.

label: Expand early messages into short exchanges
label_nl: Expand early messages into short exchanges
definition: Given a play or routine example, respond to the child’s message with one relevant word, sign, symbol, or short phrase, then leave room for another turn. Include spoken, signed, and AAC-supported communication as appropriate.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative guided play or scenario activity; not validated

assessment.method: Fictional caregiver scenario, video observation, or accessible play demonstration
criteria: models a small, relevant language expansion
preserves the child’s meaning and communication mode
supports a back-and-forth exchange without pressure

evidence_basis: ASHA early communication guidance informs this draft; communication development varies and is not a fixed age sequence.

label: Notice small quantities and changes
label_nl: Notice small quantities and changes
definition: During familiar play or routines, notice whether a small set is empty, has one item, or has more than one; compare two small sets as same, more, or fewer using objects, movement, or images.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative guided play or scenario activity; not validated

assessment.method: Guided play or a short practical demonstration with small sets and accessible materials
criteria: compares small sets using concrete objects or images
uses same, more, fewer, or none meaningfully
does not require numeral recognition

evidence_basis: Early number-sense activity informed by IES guidance on recognizing small collections and learning number through meaningful routines.

supporting_sources.title: IES — Teaching Math to Young Children: Practice Guide

label: Experience the first number words in routines
label_nl: Experience the first number words in routines
definition: Use a playful routine, rhyme, or accessible communication system to hear, see, sign, or select the number words one, two, and three in a stable sequence, without requiring a child to recite them on demand.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative guided play or scenario activity; not validated

assessment.method: Guided play or a short practical demonstration with small sets and accessible materials
criteria: models a stable short number-word sequence
accepts spoken, signed, visual, or AAC-supported access
keeps the activity playful and responsive

evidence_basis: IES foundational counting progression informs this draft. The language and modality can be adapted to the learner.

supporting_sources.title: IES — Teaching Math to Young Children: Practice Guide
IES — Teaching Math to Young Children Toolkit

label: Match one count word to one object
label_nl: Match one count word to one object
definition: With a small set of movable objects, model assigning one spoken, signed, or AAC-supported count word to each object exactly once. Begin with a small number and use pointing, eye gaze, or object movement as accessible.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative guided play or scenario activity; not validated

assessment.method: Guided play or a short practical demonstration with small sets and accessible materials
criteria: coordinates one count word or symbol with each object
avoids skipping or counting an item twice
chooses an accessible way to track counted objects

evidence_basis: IES guidance identifies one-to-one correspondence as a foundational counting principle.

supporting_sources.title: IES — Teaching Math to Young Children: Practice Guide
IES — Teaching Math to Young Children Toolkit

label: Understand that the last count gives the total
label_nl: Understand that the last count gives the total
definition: Count a small collection together, then use the final count word or symbol to answer “how many?” without recounting. Repeat with a small number of objects in varied arrangements.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative guided play or scenario activity; not validated

assessment.method: Guided play or a short practical demonstration with small sets and accessible materials
criteria: uses the final count as the total for the collection
recognizes that rearranging the same objects does not change their number
uses concrete objects or images

evidence_basis: IES guidance describes cardinality and meaningful counting as steps beyond reciting the number sequence.

supporting_sources.title: IES — Teaching Math to Young Children: Practice Guide
IES — Teaching Math to Young Children Toolkit

label: Connect a small quantity, number word, and numeral
label_nl: Connect a small quantity, number word, and numeral
definition: Match sets of one to five objects with an appropriate spoken, signed, or AAC-supported number word and a written numeral or tactile/visual representation. Use only as many symbols as are accessible to the learner.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative guided play or scenario activity; not validated

assessment.method: Guided play or a short practical demonstration with small sets and accessible materials
criteria: matches small quantities with their number words
matches the same quantities to numerals or accessible representations
distinguishes quantity from the numeral used to label it

evidence_basis: IES early mathematics guidance supports connecting counted quantities, number words, and numerals.

supporting_sources.title: IES — Teaching Math to Young Children: Practice Guide
IES — Teaching Math to Young Children Toolkit

label: Combine two small sets and count all
label_nl: Combine two small sets and count all
definition: Use counters, toys, fingers, drawings, or another accessible representation to join two small sets, then count the combined collection to find how many there are.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative guided play or scenario activity; not validated

assessment.method: Guided play or a short practical demonstration with small sets and accessible materials
criteria: represents both starting sets
combines the sets without losing or duplicating objects
counts the combined set and states or selects the total

evidence_basis: IES and What Works Clearinghouse guidance describe concrete counting strategies as an entry to simple addition.

supporting_sources.title: IES — Teaching Math to Young Children: Practice Guide

label: Represent a first addition with objects and symbols
label_nl: Represent a first addition with objects and symbols
definition: Show a small “put together” story with objects or drawings, then connect the action to a simple addition expression such as 2 + 1. Explain what each number represents and check the answer by counting the combined set.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative guided play or scenario activity; not validated

assessment.method: Guided play or a short practical demonstration with small sets and accessible materials
criteria: models the story with objects or drawings
connects each numeral and operation sign to the modeled action
checks the result with a concrete count

evidence_basis: IES early mathematics guidance supports building operations from meaningful concrete situations and representations.

supporting_sources.title: IES — Teaching Math to Young Children: Practice Guide

label: Practice supporting early communication
label_nl: Practice supporting early communication
definition: Using a fictional family scenario, choose one accessible way to follow the child’s interest, respond to an early signal, model a meaningful word, sign, or symbol, and leave time for the child’s next message. Do not treat spoken words as the only valid outcome.

estimated_active_learning_hours.basis: illustrative guided play or scenario activity; not validated

assessment.method: Fictional caregiver scenario and reflective activity design
criteria: recognizes spoken, signed, gestural, picture, and AAC communication
models language or symbols in context without requiring imitation
knows when to seek qualified communication or hearing support

evidence_basis: ASHA milestones and early-intervention AAC guidance, plus Harvard serve-and-return guidance, inform this Atlas proposal. It is not diagnosis or therapy.
